findings.title: The bump proof never ties the duel oracle baseline to the pinned duel golden
findings.claim: verifyDuelOracle accepts any baseline that exists, comes from this repo root and sits at SIM_VERSION − 1. It never checks that the baseline records the behaviour duel-1.json pins, or that the stored golden is at the baseline's version. Two cases slip through. (1) A baseline recorded after an unblessed same-version duel rule change. (2) Goldens stored two versions back (for example 36 → 38 with a baseline at 37). In both, the bump passes and `npm run bless` writes a duel-1.json holding the changed behaviour as if it were migration-only.
findings.evidence: scripts/golden/duelOracle.ts:L230-233 checks only presence, `was.cwd !== root` and `version !== was.simVersion + 1`. scripts/golden/blessGuard.ts:L18-20 computes `stale` but never compares it with the baseline's version or with currentVersion − 1. scripts/golden/versionOnly.ts:L91-96 has the same pattern for the sector (only `was.simVersion === now.simVersion` is refused). Plan L61 (Decision 12): `duel-1.json` is never re-blessed on a bump without the oracle.
findings.why: The oracle proves 'baseline equals now through the alias table', not 'the pinned golden equals now'. A red duel golden test at the baseline commit is the only remaining guard, and that guard lives outside the bless guard. So a proof gap that the guard could close itself is left to process discipline.
findings.fix: Record hashDuel every DUEL_GOLDEN_EVERY ticks in the baseline's scripted-1 run (it is the golden's run). In verifyDuelOracle, require those hashes and the baseline's simVersion to equal the stored tests/golden/duel-1.json. Alternatively, or as well, pass storedVersions through, and have blessRefusal refuse unless every stale version equals currentVersion − 1.

findings.title: Bless with every pinned artifact deleted runs neither proof
findings.claim: An absent artifact does not count as a bump. If basic.json, duel-1.json and determinism-v2.json are all missing (or the goldens are missing and the fixture is already at the current version), `stale` is empty. `npm run bless` then writes a duel golden at the new version with neither the sector proof nor the duel oracle.
findings.evidence: scripts/golden/blessGuard.ts:L15-20 says 'An absent artifact (undefined) does not count as a bump' and filters out `v !== undefined`. scripts/golden/storedVersion.ts:L22-25 returns undefined for a missing file. scripts/bless-golden.ts builds `stored` with readStoredVersion, which yields undefined for missing files. Plan L61: 'duel-1.json is never re-blessed on a bump unless the oracle…'.
findings.why: It needs a deliberate deletion, so it is unlikely. But it is the one path where a bump re-blesses the duel golden without proof, against Decision 12's 'never'.
findings.fix: Refuse when duel-1.json (or any pinned artifact) is absent unless an explicit flag such as `--fresh` is given. Or run the duel oracle whenever duel-1.json is absent.

findings.title: The oracle never checks that its schema covers the whole flattened duel
findings.claim: recordRun's length check compares the built values with the kept schema. Both come from duelSchema, so the check can never fail on a schema that is short. The check never compares against flattenDuel's actual length. If canonicalFields(layout) ever named fewer values than flatten(interior) writes, the trailing values would drop out of every per-tick and per-field digest without any error.
findings.evidence: scripts/golden/duelOracle.ts:L176-L194: `now = duelSchema(d)`; `plan.build(all.subarray(1))`; then `if (i !== values.length)`, where i and values.length both come from the schema. Only the interior's version offset is checked against `all` (L186). Today validateDuelSnapshot pins the same equality (src/renderer/src/sim/duel/snapshot.ts:L69-71), so the gap is latent.
findings.why: The prompt's question 'can any old field fall out of the oracle's comparison' should be answered by the oracle itself, not by a separate snapshot check.
findings.fix: After L185, add `if (now.counts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) !== all.length - 1) throw new Error(...)`.

findings.title: Two H-1 view spots still hard-code slot 1 as 'the other ship'
findings.claim: hitsCrew treats any laser from slot 1 as a hit on the crew. The tactical model's enemy arrow reads slot 1 directly instead of the crew's locked target. Both are correct for the duel but inconsistent with Decision 15.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/render/tactical/fxModel.ts:L34 `e.kind === 'laser' && e.ship === 1 && e.hit`. src/renderer/src/render/tactical/tacticalModel.ts:L287 `input.ships.includes(1) … interpolatedShip(state, prev, alpha, 1)`. Plan L64 (Decision 15): 'Each reads the target through targetOf where it means "the other ship"'. weaponsModel.ts and readoutModel.ts were moved to targetOf (diff L959, L694).
findings.why: Not a duel bug. It is a remaining pair assumption that R-5 would have to find again.
findings.fix: In tacticalModel L287, use `targetOf(state, 0)`. For hitsCrew, laser events carry no target, so use `e.ship !== CREW_SLOT` with a comment. Adding a target to the event can wait for R-3/R-5, because it changes the oracle's event digest.

verified: The alias table (Decisions 10 and 11, plan L59-60) is complete and not circular. In scripts/golden/duelOracle.ts:L58-78 (diff L258-276), MOVED_TO_SYSTEMS lists all 16 moved fields from Decision 2 (plan L51). Old `space.missiles.<i>` is derived from the active pool entry with owner i, as [1, ...7 flight values], or 8 zeros: the old count of 8. It matches the old MISSILE_SLOT of 8 (diff L1619-1620). Every other old name maps to itself. aliasPlan (diff L307-349) refuses an unmapped old field, a new field mapped twice, a field both derived-read and plain-mapped, a field neither mapped nor declared added, and a count change. rename is a single regex function with no chaining.

The bless guard (Decision 12): blessRefusal runs `verify`, then `duel` only if `verify` passed, and refuses on either failure (blessGuard.ts diff L139-152). `duel` is required by type. bless-golden.ts passes verifyDuelOracle (diff L105), and tests/blessGuard.test.ts L2725-2739 pins the wiring. A missing baseline, a foreign root, a same-version baseline and a non-plus-1 version are all refused (duelOracle.ts:L230-233, tested at diff L3428-3434). Mixed stored sets still count as a bump (diff L2715-2728).

Iteration order is unchanged for two slots. Ships fly in slot order (duel.ts diff L1583). Contacts run ship 0's statics, then the 0-1 pair, then ship 1's statics (contacts.ts diff L1453-1463). shipBody(map, 0, 1) and shipBody(map, 1, 0) both equal asteroids + 1, today's otherShipBody, and graceUntil keeps asteroids + 2 entries. Missiles fly, resolve, meet each other and expire in owner order through missileOf (missiles.ts diff L2129-2162). hunterThink is called once, for slot 1 (duel.ts diff L1579), so the RNG draw order is unchanged. Weapons apply and tick in slot order.

Flight arithmetic order is unchanged. In physics.ts (diff L2205-2229), `turn * cls.turnStepsPerTick * f`, `h0 * cls.thrust * f` and `h0 * cls.thrust * cls.reverseFraction * f` have the same operand order as the old tuning constants. predict.ts passes the same Engines level and class (diff L2292-2298).

Inactive slots are never stepped, collided or rendered. stepFlight, stepDuel's weapons/flight/missile/tick loops and resolveContacts skip `!active`. Missile landing skips inactive ships (missiles.ts diff L2150). laserEligible returns false for an inactive target, the firing ship itself, or an out-of-range index (weapons.ts diff L2590-2591). The duel views draw `ships: [0, 1]` (app/duel/duelMode.ts:L85). Inactive slots are hashed as zeros by design, and the validator enforces those zeros (hash.ts:L202-203).

Restore safety: validateTacticalValues (hash.ts:L190-220) runs before any allocation. It checks headingAcc in (-1, 1) for ships and missiles, so the drain loops are bounded; graceUntil as int32; skidBudget finite and ≥ 0; hull in [0, max]; that an inactive slot holds only zeros; missile `active` as 0/1; that a free entry holds only zeros (including owner); an active entry's owner as an active in-range slot; and one missile per owner. validateDuelSnapshot additionally requires two active slots, cls equal to DUEL_CLASSES[i] and target equal to 1 − i (snapshot.ts:L75-82; Decision 16, plan L65). These checks are tested, including an emptied slot 1 and two missiles for one owner (diff L3935-3956).

Unflatten writers: the bit fields refuse values other than 0/1, and `ships.length` and the asteroid count are identity checks. The missile flight writer refuses a free entry that holds values; it runs after `active` and `owner` are written (hash.ts:L39-57). cloneTacticalFromModule builds fresh containers for ships, systems and missiles (hash.ts:L143-153).

Decision 16's test holds ships.length, both active flags, the classes and the targets at every tick of the 15,772-tick scripted seed-1 run, plus two capped passive runs (tests/tacticalSlots.test.ts:L133-155). Decision 5's owner-order tests use swapped entries (tacticalSlots.test.ts:L110-130).

The H-1 local duel reads the right ship and missile. runtime.ts captures missilePrev by owner (diff L534); lock cycling reads systems[0].lock (diff L557); camera-follow uses missileOf(…, 0) (diff L571, L594). interpolatedMissile and recordTrails go by owner (fxModel.ts:L62-82). predictMissilePath flies a scratch copy keyed by owner (missilePath.ts diff L823-829). readoutModel and weaponsModel read the enemy through targetOf (diff L694-742, L959-990). Commands are still built for slot 0 and admitted through canCharge and canLaunch (step.ts:L104-112).
No source file still treats `state.missiles[i]` as nullable. A grep over src shows only hash.ts accessors and state.ts helpers, so no always-truthy pool-entry check remains.

Definitions (Decision 7): CUTTER_CLASS and HUNTER_CLASS carry today's tuning numbers, power is null, and both are frozen (defs.ts:L44-66). systems[i].cls is hashed. HUNTER_* tuning stays in tuning.ts. hunterSlot picks the active, non-crew slot whose class has the hunter AI profile (duel.ts diff L1558-1560; Decision 8).

Decision 15's pairs are kept. Telemetry keeps `[crew, enemy] = tac.ships` and its two-iteration loops, and moves laserOn to targetOf (telemetry.ts diff L1302-1311). The bait check `k > asteroids` equals the old `k === asteroids + 1` for two slots (diff L1328-1331). The duel checkpoint's telemetry grace length now comes from graceUntil.length (duelCheckpoint.ts diff L628).

Boundaries: the changed sim files use only Math.abs, min, max, sign, sqrt and floor. Math.max with a spread is still Math.max. There are no platform globals. defs.ts imports only tuning (tests/helpers/determinismGuard.ts:L3, L33).
The checkpoint's outcome index `values[1 + 4]` is still `outcome`, because ships.length is appended after it (hash.ts:L66-72; duelCheckpoint.ts diff L621).
not_verified: No tests, typecheck, oracle runs, gates or cross-engine checks were run (read-only; Jest/Vitest not run). The claims of 20 runs and 205,178 identical ticks, of gate outcomes of 7 wins, 3 losses and a median of 251.2 s, and of a passing suite are taken from the brief.
The generated tests/golden/*.json and tests/fixtures/*.json were not inspected (excluded from the diff by design).
